elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Client may assign or transfer this Agreement ... without the prior written approval of TrueLink, to a financially responsible affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in interest by way of merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights or obligations ... without the prior written approval of Client, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "No change of control of Client shall constitute an assignment or give rise to any right of TrueLink to terminate ... this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Client successor carve-out plus "Any other assignment or transfer shall require the prior written approval of the other party" (Vendor successor assignment only on consent, but mutual consent framework present)

elements.element: Written notice requirement for successor assignments
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears; clause is silent on notice

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Any other assignment or transfer shall require the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

offending_extra_words: or of the business to which this Agreement relates
Any other assignment or transfer shall require the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.
reasons: All five atomic preferred elements are satisfied by the operative text, so the locked preferred level is complete.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no written-notice mechanic), but that is irrelevant since preferred is met and the levels must not be blended.

Minimality fails: the edit is a whole-clause rewrite expanding 37 words to 139 (ratio 3.76) with an 0.800 changed-character ratio, both above the official gates. The original 'Neither party shall assign ... without prior written approval ... except ... affiliate' could have been retained as the anchor, with a Customer successor carve-out, a reasonableness qualifier, a competitor bar, and a short change-of-control sentence inserted.

Specific surplus language: 'reorganization' and 'or of the business to which this Agreement relates' broaden the carve-out beyond the playbook; 'suspend or re-price' adds protection beyond the required no-termination-on-change-of-control point; 'shall constitute an assignment or' is a second, duplicative deeming mechanic; and the standalone 'Any other assignment' sentence duplicates the consent standard already imposed on TrueLink and imports fallback-style drafting.
Intent preserved: the mutual consent baseline and the pre-existing affiliate carve-out survive, no defined term is left dangling, and no unrelated commercial term is disturbed.
